plans.objective: [DIM: optimization] The apparent flatness of N_c(w) for rigid families is an optimization artifact: small networks get stuck in local minima and fail to find the low-dimensional solution, making the problem appear "fat" (capacity required) when it is actually rigid.

steps.description: Implement the family function defining rigid (low-dimensional) and fat (high-dimensional) constraint families for the capacity scan experiment. The rigid family will be a linear constraint (1D solution space), while the fat family will be a sinusoidal constraint with multiple parameters (higher-dimensional solution space). This implements the core scientific logic needed to test whether small networks get stuck in local minima, making rigid problems appear "fat" (requiring more capacity) than they truly are.

plans.objective: [DIM: optimization] The apparent flatness of N_c(w) for rigid families is an optimization artifact: small networks get stuck in local minima and fail to find zero-violation solutions even when they exist, causing N_c(w) to appear artificially flat or increasing.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the family function for the rigid linear constraint family (linear function f(x)=ax+b) to provide a provable low-dimensional, unique solution space. This will serve as a "zero-violation anchor" (Step 0) to validate that the experimental setup can achieve zero-violation with sufficient width, before scanning N_c(w). The linear family ensures the optimization landscape is convex and free of local minima traps, isolating whether any observed flatness in N_c(w) for other families is an optimization artifact or a property of the constraint space itself.
